mainTopic: Where does רב הונא's rule come from, that a sale made under pressure (תלוהו וזבין) still counts? The גמרא tries two proofs from forced consent, rejects both, and grounds the rule in logic. רב יהודה then challenges it from the law of a forced גט.
overview: This amud continues the search for a source for רב הונא's rule: if someone was strung up until he agreed to sell, the sale is valid. The גמרא brings a ברייתא about pressuring a man until he says 'I want to' bring his קרבן, and then the same ברייתא's ending about a forced גט. It rejects both, because in each case the man really wants something: כפרה, or obeying the חכמים. So the rule rests on סברא: because of the pressure, he makes up his mind and sells. רב יהודה challenges this from a גט forced by non-Jews, and רב משרשיא answers that such a גט is valid by Torah law and only invalid by rabbinic decree. רב המנונא challenges from the סיקריקון case. רב answers that the sale is void only without a שטר, and שמואל agrees a forced sale counts when money was paid. A challenge from רב ביבי's line in the name of רב נחמן is answered by saying רב הונא simply disagrees with that אמורא's statement. Finally רבא rules that a forced sale is valid and begins to limit the rule, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from forcing someone to bring his promised offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a man who promised a עולה is pressured until he says 'I want to.' This suggests that agreement given under pressure counts as real agreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'He shall offer it.' This teaches that we force him to bring it. Could it mean we take it against his will? No, because the פסוק says 'according to his will.' So how do both fit? We pressure him until he says, 'I want to.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers its first source for רב הונא's rule. It cites a ברייתא showing that a 'yes' produced by pressure is treated as a real 'yes.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say two opposite things: 'offer it' (force him) and 'according to his will' (he must want it). The ברייתא solves this by saying we pressure him until he agrees, and that agreement counts. If forced agreement counts for a קרבן, maybe it also counts for a forced sale.

keyTerms.meaning: We force him (the court pressures him)
Against his will
According to his will / willingly
So how can this be? (used to reconcile two sources)
I want to

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying we take the animal and offer it ourselves. The man himself must end up saying 'I want to'; the pressure only gets him to that point.

phrases.english: "He shall offer it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:3, about someone who pledged a burnt-offering.

phrases.english: teaches that we force him.
Could it mean against his will?
The verse says: "according to his will."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, a few words later.

phrases.english: How can both be true?
We force him until he says:
"I want to."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier search for a source for רב הונא's rule that a sale under pressure is valid.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that agreement produced by pressure counts as real agreement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on ויקרא 1:3: we pressure the man until he says 'I want to' bring his קרבן.

steps.title: Rejecting the offering proof: he really wants atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof aside. With a קרבן, deep down the man truly wants כפרה, so his 'yes' is genuine. A seller under pressure may not truly want to sell.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is different there, because he is happy to get atonement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first proof. It argues that the קרבן case is special and cannot be applied to a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the קרבן, the pressure only uncovers what he already wanted inside, which is כפרה. A forced seller has no such hidden wish to sell. So the קרבן case does not prove that a truly forced 'yes' counts.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
It is different there
He is pleased with it / it suits him
Atonement

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since he is glad to have atonement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself. The rule of רב הונא is not disproven, only left without this source.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the קרבן case the man truly wants כפרה deep down, which a forced seller lacks.

steps.title: Second proof: forcing a husband to give a divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the end of the same ברייתא: a husband ordered to divorce is pressured until he says 'I want to,' and the גט works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from the end of the ברייתא: 'And so too with divorce documents: we force him until he says, I want to.'
steps.whatsHappening: After the first proof failed, the גמרא tries a second one from the end of the same source. Here there is no כפרה involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband being forced to divorce has no obvious inner wish like כפרה. Even so, his pressured 'I want to' makes the גט valid. That looks like a better match for a forced sale.

keyTerms.meaning: From the latter part (of the source)
Divorce documents of women
And so too you say (the same rule applies)

phrases.english: But rather, from the latter part:
phrases.notes: He means the end of the same ברייתא just quoted.

phrases.english: And so too you say regarding divorce documents –
phrases.notes: This is a case where the court has ruled that he must divorce.

phrases.english: we force him until he says: "I want to."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of step 1 with a new one from the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that agreement produced by pressure counts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: End of the ברייתא: a forced husband says 'I want to' and the גט is valid.

steps.title: Rejecting the divorce proof: he wants to obey the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this proof too. A Jew truly wants to fulfill the מצוה of listening to the חכמים, so his 'yes' to the גט is genuine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is different there, because it is a מצוה to listen to the words of the חכמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second proof the same way as the first. The divorce case has a special reason that a sale does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the חכמים rule that he must divorce, his deeper wish is to do the מצוה of obeying them. So the pressure reveals a real desire. A forced seller has no מצוה pushing him to sell.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to listen to the words of the Sages

phrases.english: But perhaps it is different there,
since it is a מצוה to listen to the words of the Sages!

steps.triggerLanguage: ודלמא שאני התם דמצוה לשמוע דברי חכמים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the divorce case the husband truly wants to obey the חכמים, which gives his 'yes' real backing that a forced seller lacks.

steps.title: The rule is based on logic: pressure makes him decide
steps.stepSummary: Since no text proves it, the גמרא says רב הונא's rule is simple סברא. Because of the pressure, the seller makes a real decision and transfers the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is logic: because of the pressure on him, he makes up his mind and transfers ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops looking for a written source. It says רב הונא's rule comes from logical reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that pressure does not cancel a decision; it causes one. Once he gives in, he truly decides to sell, so the sale is valid. This is a sound reason in its own right and needs no פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical reasoning
Because of his being forced
He decides fully and transfers ownership

steps.whatToRemember: Two proofs from forced consent (the קרבן and the גט) were rejected, because each had a hidden real desire behind it. רב הונא's rule stands on סברא: אגב אונסיה גמר ומקנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that a pressured sale is a real sale, becomes the basis for the rest of the סוגיא and for the הלכה of forced sales.

phrases.english: Rather, it is logic –
because of his being forced, he decides and transfers ownership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both proofs fail, the גמרא gives a logical basis instead.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sale made under pressure is valid because the pressure leads him to truly decide to sell (אגב אונסיה גמר ומקנה).

steps.title: רב יהודה's challenge from a divorce forced by non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה cites a משנה: a גט forced by a Jewish court is valid, but one forced by non-Jews is invalid. If pressure leads to a real decision, why should the non-Jews' pressure fail?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה objects: A forced גט: if forced by Jews, it is valid; if by non-Jews, it is invalid. But with non-Jews, they may beat him and say, 'Do what the Jew tells you.' Why is it invalid? There too, let us say that because of the pressure he decides and divorces!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה attacks the logic just given, using a משנה about a forced גט. The step closes by asking why the logic of step 5 does not apply there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being forced creates a real decision, it should not matter who did the forcing. Yet the משנה says a גט forced by a non-Jewish court on its own is invalid. That seems to show forced consent does not automatically count.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection
A forced divorce document
Valid / invalid
They beat him
But why?

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does allow non-Jews to apply pressure when they say 'Do what the Jew tells you.' Then the Jewish court is really behind it. What is invalid is non-Jews forcing a גט on their own authority.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda objects:
A forced divorce document:
if by Jews, it is valid,
and if by non-Jews, it is invalid.
And with non-Jews, they may beat him,
and say to him:
Do what the Jew tells you.
But why?
phrases.notes: He is asking why the non-Jews' own forced גט is invalid.

phrases.english: There too, let us say:
because of his being forced, he decides and divorces!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logical principle concluded in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The סברא of אגב אונסיה גמר ומקנה supporting רב הונא's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If pressure creates real consent, a גט forced by non-Jews should also be valid. The משנה rules it invalid, which suggests forced consent does not automatically count.

steps.title: A forced גט from non-Jews is really valid by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says a גט forced by גוים is valid by Torah law. The חכמים only made it invalid so women would not use גוים to escape their husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about this משנה that רב משרשיא said: By Torah law, a גט forced even by non-Jews is valid. So why did the חכמים say a גט forced by non-Jews is invalid? So that not every woman will go and put herself in the hands of a non-Jew and free herself from her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6. It shows that the משנה's rule against a גט forced by גוים is not a Torah rule. It is a rabbinic safeguard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the גט from גוים is invalid because the pressure did not produce a real decision. רב משרשיא shows that by Torah law the husband's decision under pressure does count, exactly as רב הונא says. The invalidity is only a rabbinic fence against abuse, so רב הונא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law, as opposed to a rabbinic rule
Valid / invalid
Puts herself in the hands of, relies on (someone)
Frees herself, releases herself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that pressure from גוים fails to produce a real decision. By Torah law it does work. The גט is invalid only because of a rabbinic decree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer separates the Torah-level logic (pressure still leads to a real decision) from a rabbinic policy concern. That separation is what saves רב הונא's rule.

phrases.english: Wasn't it already stated about it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה about a forced גט that was quoted in Step 6.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
By Torah law, even if forced by non-Jews it is valid,
So why did they say that when forced by non-Jews it is invalid?

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת
phrases.english: So that it should not be that each and every woman
goes and places herself in the hand of a non-Jew,
and frees herself from her husband's hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's challenge from Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the rule: the invalidity is rabbinic, not Torah-level.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גט forced by גוים is invalid because the pressure did not create a real decision.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law it is valid, because pressure does create a real decision. The חכמים invalidated it only to stop abuse.

steps.title: Challenge from buying land after a violent seizer
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא points to the משנה: if someone buys a field from a סיקריקון and then buys it again from the original owner, the sale is void. Why isn't the owner's sale under pressure considered a real decision?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objected: If someone bought a field from a violent seizer, and then went back and bought it from the original owner, his purchase is void. But why? There too, let us say that because of the pressure he decided and transferred it!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to רב הונא. A משנה voids a sale made by an owner under pressure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original owner sold his field because it had already been taken from him by force, so he was under pressure. If רב הונא is right that pressure leads to a real decision, this sale should work. Yet the משנה says it is void.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, challenges
A violent man who seized land by threats
The original owner
His purchase is void
Because of the pressure, he decides and transfers. This is רב הונא's reasoning

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna objected:
If one bought a field from a violent seizer,
and then went back and bought it from the original owner,
his purchase is void.
But why? There too let us say:
because of his pressure he decides and transfers!
phrases.notes: This is exactly רב הונא's reasoning from Step 5, used here against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב הונא from the גט challenge, the גמרא faces a second challenge from a sale case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that a sale made under pressure is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner of the seized field sold under pressure, yet the משנה voids the sale. That contradicts the idea that pressure leads to a real decision.

steps.title: רב limits the void sale to a case with no document
steps.stepSummary: רב says the sale is void only when the owner just said 'go take possession.' If he wrote a שטר, the buyer acquires the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about this, that רב said: They only taught this when the owner told him 'Go take possession and acquire.' But if there was a document, he acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב המנונא by quoting רב. The משנה's void sale applies only to a narrow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a שטר, the owner can say he never really meant to sell. He was just letting the buyer try his luck against the seizer. With a שטר, his decision is real and the sale works, which fits רב הונא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of
Go take possession and acquire. The owner only gave verbal permission
A written document, here a bill of sale
He acquires

phrases.english: Wasn't it stated about it: Rav said:
They only taught this where he said to him:
"Go take possession and acquire,"
but with a document, he acquires.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה voids every sale from the owner after a seizure.
steps.terutzMaskana: It voids the sale only without a שטר. With a שטר the sale is valid, in line with רב הונא.

steps.title: What about שמואל, who voids even a sale with a document?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds the buyer does not acquire even with a שטר. So how does רב הונא's rule fit שמואל's view?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, who says that even with a document he does not acquire, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. רב's answer works, but שמואל disagrees with רב, so the challenge comes back on his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the owner's sale under pressure fails even with a שטר. That seems to go against רב הונא's rule that pressure leads to a real sale. The גמרא asks how to explain this according to שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Even with a document too
What can be said? (How do we answer?)

phrases.english: And according to Shmuel, who said:
even with a document he does not acquire,
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב's answer does not work according to שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule, as it fits with שמואל's opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל voids the sale even with a שטר, so it seems that, in his view, pressure does not lead to a real sale.

steps.title: שמואל agrees when money was paid
steps.stepSummary: שמואל agrees the sale is valid when the buyer paid money, which is the case in רב הונא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל agrees in a case where the buyer gave money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל's strict view does not apply when money was paid. The next step challenges this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיקריקון case, the original owner did not receive real payment for his field. In רב הונא's case, the seller under pressure was paid. שמואל agrees that when money is received, the pressured seller truly decides to sell.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes
Money (literally, zuz coins)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's rule survives every challenge. A sale or גט made under pressure is valid because the person ends up truly deciding. The forced גט from גוים is invalid only by rabbinic decree. The סיקריקון case is void only without a שטר (רב), or without payment (שמואל).

phrases.english: Shmuel agrees where he gave money.
phrases.notes: In רב הונא's case the seller was paid, so even שמואל would agree that sale is valid.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: payment versus no payment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל rejects any sale made under pressure.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל agrees that a pressured sale is valid when money was paid, as in רב הונא's case.

steps.title: Challenge from רב ביבי's report of רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי ends רב הונא's own teaching (תליוהו וזבין) with a line in the name of רב נחמן: the one who forced the sale has no right to the land, but he does have a right to his money back. That implies he paid, and the sale is still void. How does that fit what was just said?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב ביבי, who ends this teaching with a line in the name of רב נחמן, "He has no land, but he has money", what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer, which said a forced sale counts when money was paid. רב ביבי's line seems to show that even when money was paid, the buyer still does not get the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "He has money" means the owner must give the forcing buyer his money back, so that buyer must have paid for the field. Even so, he gets no land. That goes straight against the idea that paying money makes a forced sale valid, which was the basis for fitting רב הונא's rule in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Who ends it with (adds a closing line to the teaching)
He has no right to the land
He has a right to the money (he gets paid back)
What can be said? (a formula for a hard question)

phrases.english: And according to רב ביבי,
who ends it with a line in the name of רב נחמן:
phrases.notes: "It" is רב הונא's own teaching that a sale made after being strung up is valid.

phrases.english: he has no land,
phrases.notes: "He" is the one who forced the owner to sell.

phrases.english: but he has money,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב בִּיבִי, דִּמְסַיֵּים בַּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 11's claim that paying money makes the forced sale valid
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that a sale under pressure is valid when money was paid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ביבי's line shows the forcing buyer paid, since he gets his money back, yet he still gets no land. So paying money does not make the sale valid.

steps.title: רב הונא disagrees with רב ביבי's statement
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי's line is only the statement of an אמורא, and רב הונא, also an אמורא, does not hold like it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי's line is an אמורא's statement, and רב הונא does not agree with that statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב ביבי's line is not a ruling from a משנה or ברייתא. It is only one אמורא's view, and רב הונא is allowed to disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא cannot argue with a תנא, but he can argue with another אמורא. Since רב ביבי's line is just a מימרא, it does not disprove רב הונא. The two simply hold different views.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement of an אמורא, not a source from the time of the תנאים
He does not hold of it (he disagrees)

phrases.english: רב ביבי's line is an אמורא's statement,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵימְרָא לְרַב הוּנָא לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and רב הונא does not hold of that statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב ביבי in step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: מחלוקת between אמוראים: the challenging source does not bind רב הונא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ביבי's line seemed to be an authority that disproves רב הונא's rule
steps.terutzMaskana: It is only an אמורא's view, so רב הונא may disagree, and his rule stands
steps.whatToRemember: A challenge from another אמורא's statement can be answered by saying the two אמוראים simply disagree. Only a משנה or ברייתא would bind רב הונא.

steps.title: רבא rules that a forced sale is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבא states the הלכה: if someone was hung up until he agreed to sell, his sale is valid. He then begins to limit this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is, if they hung him up and he sold, his sale is a valid sale. And we only said this...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the practical הלכה: a sale made under even severe pressure still counts. He then begins to add a limit, and the rest of that limit comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the סוגיא in favor of the idea that a forced sale counts, the same idea we saw with רב הונא. The words "ולא אמרן אלא" tell us an exception is coming, so the rule is not finished yet.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical law
They hung him up and he sold (a sale made under force)
His sale is a valid sale
And we only said this when... (opens a limit on the rule)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at "his sale is valid". רבא is about to limit the rule to a specific case, and that limit continues right after this line.

phrases.english: רבא said: The הלכה is:
if they hung him up and he sold,
his sale is a valid sale.
And we only said this...
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where רבא gives the case he means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב הונא's rule, the גמרא gives רבא's final הלכה, which agrees that a forced sale counts
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sale made under force is valid. A limit on this rule follows.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for sales made under pressure, and it shapes how the rest of the סוגיא treats forced deals.
